card.title: Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Sequences impose patterns; series sum them. **AP** (constant difference): aₙ = a + (n−1)d and **Sₙ = n/2(a + l)** — Gauss's forward–backward pairing proves it in one line. **GP** (constant ratio): aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹, Sₙ = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1), and the **sum to infinity S∞ = a/(1 − r) exists iff |r| < 1** — the fate of rⁿ is the whole story (8 − 4 + 2 − 1 + ⋯ with r = −½ sums to 16/3). **HP** hides an AP in the reciprocals.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
AP: aₙ = a + (n−1)d; Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n−1)d] = n/2(a + l)
GP: aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹; Sₙ = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1); S∞ = a/(1−r) iff |r| < 1
AM = (a+b)/2 ≥ GM = √(ab) ≥ HM = 2ab/(a+b); AM·HM = GM²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x HP has a direct sum formula. x Take reciprocals, use AP sum.  ·  x r can be any value in infinite GP. x Must have |r| < 1 for convergence.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A harmonic progression has no sum formula of its own: take reciprocals, sum the resulting AP, and the sum of the HP is the sum of the reciprocals of those partial sums.  ·  If r = 1 the GP is constant with S_n = na, and the formula carrying (r - 1) in the denominator is undefined.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Gauss's pairing*** - write the AP sum forwards and backwards; every column pairs to a + l, giving S_n = n(a + l)/2 without any algebra.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: x AM = GM always. x AM >= GM, equality only when all terms equal.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Find the nth term and the sum of the first n terms of a given AP, having first identified a and d, or the last term l, from the listed terms.  ·  Find the nth term and the sum to n terms of a GP, having first identified the common ratio by dividing any term by the one before it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: AP sum: pair first and last. GP S_inf: check |r| < 1 first. Means insertion: count terms then solve for d or r. AM-GM: expand (a - b)^2 >= 0.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): The sum of the first 10 terms of an AP is 175 and its first term is 5. Find the common difference and the 10th term.** — **Sum formula:** S₁₀ = n/2[2a + (n−1)d] = (10/2)[2(5) + 9d] = 5(10 + 9d). **Set equal:** 5(10 + 9d) = 175 ⟹ 10 + 9d = 35 ⟹ **d = 25/9**. **Tenth term:** a₁₀ = a + 9d = 5 + 9(25/9) = 5 + 25 = **30**.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Find the sum to infinity of the geometric series 8 − 4 + 2 − 1 + ⋯** — **Step 1 — ratio:** r = (−4)/8 = **−1/2**. **Step 2 — convergence check:** |r| = 1/2 < 1 ✓ — the necessary licence for using S∞; without it the formula is meaningless. **Step 3 — formula:** S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 8/(1 − (−½)) = 8/(3/2) = **16/3 ≈ 5.33**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For S_inf questions, write the convergence check |r| < 1 as a separate line - it is a mark even when the arithmetic is trivial.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Convergence hangs on r^n: |r| < 1 kills it, and only then does a/(1 - r) mean anything - the formula is licensed by the limit, not the other way round.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: AP: a_n = a + (n-1)d; S_n = n/2[2a + (n-1)d] = n/2(a + l); arithmetic mean b = (a + c)/2. GP: a_n = ar^(n-1); S_n = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1); sum to infinity S_inf = a/(1 - r) iff |r| < 1; geometric mean b^2 = ac. HP: reciprocals form an AP.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Zeno's paradox dissolves in S_inf = a/(1 - r): infinitely many steps, finite total distance - 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... = 1.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Insert three arithmetic means between 4 and 16, and verify the block.** — The sequence 4, A₁, A₂, A₃, 16 must be an AP with first term a = 4, fifth term 16, so 5 terms total. **Solve for d:** a₅ = a + 4d ⟹ 16 = 4 + 4d ⟹ **d = 3**.…

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The 20th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, ... is → B  ·  The sum to infinity of the series 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + ... is → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Progress With a Pattern A **sequence** is an ordered list with a rule; a **series** is its sum. The theorems: the AP nth-term and sum formulas, the GP nth-term, sum and **sum to infinity**, the AM–GM–HM ordering, and the special sums Σn, Σn², Σn³.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Arithmetic progression (AP) - Constant difference d: aₙ = a + (n−1)d; **sum Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n−1)d] = n/2(a + l)** (l = last term). - **Arithmetic mean:** the middle term of any three-term AP block: b = (a + c)/2. ### 2.2 Geometric progression (GP) - Constant ratio r: aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹; **sum Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1)** (r ≠ 1).…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **AP** | Constant difference d | 3, 7, 11, … (d = 4) | | **GP** | Constant ratio r | 2, 6, 18, … (r = 3) | | **S∞** | Limit of GP partial sums, |r| < 1 | 1 + ½ + ¼ + ⋯ = 2 | | **AM–GM–HM** | The three means, ordered | AM ≥ GM ≥ HM |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Σi = n(n+1)/2; Σi² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; Σi³ = [n(n+1)/2]²  ·  Negative or zero r still give a valid finite sum formula, but the series diverges to infinity unless |r| < 1.  ·  AM = GM = HM only when every number is equal, so a strict inequality A > G > H is the signal that the numbers are not identical.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Arithmetic mean is always defined, but GM needs non-negative numbers and HM needs non-zero numbers, since the means are taken over reciprocals.  ·  No verified PYQ on this row exists in the bank; all items here are NEB-style practice.  ·  "S_inf = a/(1 - r) iff |r| < 1; AM >= GM >= HM with equality iff a = b; sum i^3 = [n(n+1)/2]^2."

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the AP sum formula works - Write S forwards and backwards and add: each column sums to a + l, and there are n columns — Gauss's pairing argument gives Sₙ = n(a + l)/2.…
